Subject: MAP draft: ACME POC environment dependencies (VPC peering, allowlists, SSO, KMS)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion I put together a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft focused on the POC environment setup items that will unblock the technical demo. Key milestone we want to confirm now is “POC environment ready (network + auth + secrets)” so Redwood can deploy the model and run the POC tests.

High-level MAP items (draft):
- POC env provisioning: VPC peering or secure private connectivity (owner: Acme IT / Redwood Infra)
- IP allowlists: egress/ingress ranges for Redwood endpoints (owner: Acme Networking)
- SSO / SAML: IdP metadata + test account (owner: Acme Security)
- Secrets / KMS: KMS key access or Redwood-managed secrets approach (owner: Acme Security / DevOps)

Target dates (proposal):
- Provide networking details & SAML metadata: by 2026-04-07
- Complete VPC peering + allowlist config: by 2026-04-14
- Secrets/KMS access validated: by 2026-04-21
- POC environment verification & handoff: by 2026-04-24
- POC close / target decision date: 2026-04-30

Asks for Acme today:
1) Confirm owners for each milestone (names & emails)
2) Share IdP metadata XML (SAML) and a test user to exercise SSO
3) Share VPC / account info (AWS account ID, VPC CIDR) or let us know if you prefer static IP allowlist instead of peering
4) Confirm whether you require customer-managed KMS or we can use Redwood-managed secrets for the POC

I attached the MAP draft (acme-map-draft-20260330.pdf) and included the items above. Dev, Rishi — please review the tech asks and add specifics we need from Acme (I'll update the MAP after we hear back). Jordan / Sara — pinging you for owners + timing.

Thanks,

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP draft: ACME POC environment dependencies (VPC peering, allowlists, SSO, KMS)

Hi Jordan / team —

Quick technical checklist from Redwood Infra for the POC networking & auth items. I’m attaching a short tech-spec but listing the minimum required here so you can pass to Sara / Sam.

VPC peering (preferred for low-latency/private traffic):
- Needed from Acme: AWS account ID, VPC ID (vpc-xxxx), VPC CIDR (e.g., 10.20.0.0/16), preferred region (us-west-2)
- Redwood will provide: VPC ID to accept peering, route table update instructions, and the peering connection ID once initiated
- Note: Both sides must add routes to route tables for the peer CIDR; Security groups should allow the relevant ports (HTTPS 443 for API)

IP allowlist (alternative):
- If you prefer allowlist-only, provide the exact CIDR ranges you will accept and we will confirm Redwood egress IPs. For the POC we can provide a stable set of egress ranges (IPv4): 34.210.45.0/24, 52.23.128.0/24 (these are example placeholders — we will provide final ranges in writing).

SSO / SAML:
- We support SAML 2.0. Please provide IdP metadata XML and the test user email.
- ACS URL (Redwood): https://auth.redwood.ai/saml/acs
- Attributes we expect: email, firstName, lastName, and groups (optional).

Secrets / KMS:
- Redwood supports both Redwood-managed secrets (fastest for POC) and customer-managed KMS (we can accept grant-based access to a CMK). If you require CMK, please provide the ARN and a cross-account grant or the AWS principal we should use (we will coordinate minimal IAM permissions).

Other notes:
- If you need a small network test before peering, we can spin up a test endpoint reachable over the public internet and validate connectivity from your side.
- For the initial POC we recommend Redwood-managed secrets unless compliance requires CMK — that reduces setup time by several days.

I’ve attached the tech checklist (acme-technical-spec-peering-20260331.pdf). Happy to jump on a 15-min call with Sara / Sam to walk through the peering steps if helpful — I’m available tomorrow 10:00-12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
